faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to the most common questions about our programs and teaching approach.
faq.q1: What is the appropriate age range for QudSchool programs?
faq.a1: Our programs are designed for children aged 6 to 18, with different curricula suited to each age and skill level.
faq.q2: Do the programs require prior programming experience?
faq.a2: Not at all! We start from scratch with beginners, and we also have advanced programs for students with prior experience.
faq.q3: How do students communicate with teachers?
faq.a3: We provide live interactive online sessions, plus support through our learning platform and email.
faq.a4: Yes, we grant accredited certificates upon successfully completing each program, which help students in their educational and professional journey.
faq.a5: All you need is a computer or laptop and a stable internet connection. We provide all necessary tools and software.
faq.q6: Can I try the programs before subscribing?
faq.a6: Absolutely! We offer a free trial session for each program so you can experience the teaching style and curriculum before subscribing.

support.article.gettingStarted.title: Getting Started with Code School
support.article.gettingStarted.subtitle: Your guide to starting your learning journey.
support.article.gettingStarted.content.p: Welcome to Code School! We're thrilled to have you. The best place to start is our Courses page, where you can browse our full catalog. Use the filters to find topics that interest you. Once enrolled, your courses will appear in the 'My Learning' section.

Your Dashboard is your personal hub. It shows your progress, recommended courses, and recent activity. Don't forget to check out the AI Tutor for instant help with coding questions and the Study Zone for gamified learning with flashcards.
support.article.accountManagement.title: Managing Your Account
support.article.accountManagement.subtit: Keep your personal information up to date.
support.article.accountManagement.conten: You can update your personal information, including your name and bio, from your Profile page. Click on your avatar in the top-right corner and select 'My Profile'.
To change your password, language preferences, or notification settings, navigate to the Settings page. For security reasons, you may be asked to re-enter your current password to make changes.
support.article.billing.title: Billing and Subscriptions
support.article.billing.subtitle: Manage your payment and subscription details.
support.article.billing.content.p1: All subscription management is handled through the Settings page under the (future) 'Billing' tab. There you can update your payment method, view invoices, and change or cancel your plan.
support.article.billing.content.p2: If you cancel your Pro plan, you will retain Pro access until the end of your current billing period. Afterwards, your account will be downgraded to the Basic plan.

support.article.technical.subtitle: Solutions for common problems.
support.article.technical.content.p1: If you are experiencing issues with video playback, please try clearing your browser cache or using a different browser. Our platform is optimized for the latest versions of Chrome, Firefox, and Safari.
support.article.technical.content.p2: For any other technical problems or to report a bug, please use the 'Contact Us' form at the bottom of this page. Provide as much detail as possible, including your browser, operating system, and a description of the issue.

flashcards.decks.react.title: React Basics
flashcards.decks.react.desc: Fundamental concepts and hooks for React beginners.
flashcards.decks.react.a1: JSX stands for JavaScript XML. It's a syntax extension that allows you to write HTML-like code in your JavaScript files.
flashcards.decks.react.a2: A React hook that lets you add state to functional components. It returns a stateful value and a function to update it.
flashcards.decks.react.q3: What is the difference between a component and an element?
flashcards.decks.react.a3: A component is a blueprint or a template (a function or a class). An element is the object that gets returned from a component, describing what to render.
flashcards.decks.dsa.title: Data Structures
flashcards.decks.dsa.desc: Key data structures for technical interviews.
flashcards.decks.dsa.a1: A linear data structure that stores a collection of elements, each identified by at least one array index or key.
flashcards.decks.dsa.a2: A linear data structure where elements are not stored at contiguous memory locations but are linked using pointers.

faqPage.hero.subtitle: Direct answers to the most common questions about QudSchool.
faqPage.a.whatIs: QudSchool is an AI-powered educational platform teaching children and youth programming, computer science, robotics, and game development in Arabic and English.
faqPage.q.ages: What ages does the platform serve?
faqPage.a.ages: We serve children from primary stage through teens, with progressive tracks by age and level.
faqPage.a.languages: Arabic is the default language, and English is fully supported with complete RTL and LTR support.
faqPage.a.courses: We offer courses in programming basics, web development, game development, robotics and STEM, artificial intelligence, computer science, and creative computing.
faqPage.q.duration: How long does each course take?

faqPage.a.refund: Yes, you can request a full refund within 7 days of subscription if you're not satisfied.

blogPage.hero.title: Blog
blogPage.hero.subtitle: Articles and educational guides from the QudSchool team on teaching programming and AI.
blogPost.cta.title: Enjoyed This Article?
blogPost.cta.desc: Start your child's programming journey with QudSchool.
blog.post.1.title: Why Should Your Child Learn Programming in 2026?
blog.post.1.excerpt: In an era dominated by AI, programming has become a core skill like reading and writing. Discover why now is the perfect time.
blog.post.1.content:
Programming has become the most in-demand skill in the modern job market, but its benefits extend far beyond careers.
When a child learns programming, they don't just gain a technical skill — they develop systematic logical thinking that helps in every area of life.
Programming teaches patience and perseverance. The child learns that mistakes are a natural part of the process, and that every problem has a solution if tackled in order.
At QudSchool, we believe early starts give children great confidence. Children who learn programming at a young age excel academically in math and science.
It's not just about preparing children to become programmers, but to become thinkers, innovators, and leaders in whatever field they choose.
blog.post.2.title: AI for Kids: A Practical Guide to Getting Started
blog.post.2.excerpt: AI is not just a future technology — it's part of our children's lives today. Here's a practical guide to start teaching them.
blog.post.2.content:
AI is no longer a vague or complex technical concept — it has become a daily tool children use without realizing.
Teaching a child AI basics means introducing them to how intelligent systems work, how machines learn, and where we see them in daily life.
The ideal start is with simple questions: How does the app know you like this video? How does the camera translate text? How does a computer play chess?
Then we move to simple practical projects, like training a model to recognize images or sounds.
At QudSchool we offer the AI Classroom program that takes students from zero to building small AI projects in a simplified, fun way.
blog.post.3.title: Game Development for Beginners: From Idea to Project
blog.post.3.excerpt: Game development combines programming, creativity, and art. Learn how your child can start this exciting journey.
blog.post.3.content:
Game development is one of the most attractive fields for children, combining programming, design, and creative thinking.
When a child develops a game, they think as producer, developer, and tester at the same time — developing multiple skills in one project.
The start is with simple tools like Scratch to learn programming logic, then we move to Unity or other engines.
Children learn to break big problems into small steps — an essential skill in programming and engineering.
At QudSchool, every student in the game development program graduates with a complete game project they can share with family and friends.
blog.post.4.title: Robotics for Kids: A Bridge Between Code and the Physical World
blog.post.4.excerpt: Robotics turns code into something tangible. That's what makes it such a powerful learning tool for children.
blog.post.4.content:
Robotics combines programming, engineering, and electronics, making learning a fully dimensional experience.
When a child sees the code they wrote move a real robot, they feel the joy of real accomplishment.
This type of learning builds a deep connection between abstract thinking and practical application.
Robotics also teaches children teamwork, problem-solving, and dealing with real constraints like space, power, and time.
The robotics program at QudSchool gives students the chance to build and program real robots in a safe, educational environment.
